Find links on a page

Source: R/read-html.R
ragnar_find_links.Rd

Find links on a page

Usage

ragnar_find_links(
  x,
  depth = 0L,
  children_only = FALSE,
  progress = TRUE,
  ...,
  url_filter = identity,
  validate = FALSE,
  get_timestamps = FALSE,
  include_root = FALSE,
  metadata = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

URL, HTML file path, or XML document. For Markdown, convert to HTML using commonmark::markdown_html() first.

depth

Integer specifying how many levels deep to crawl for links. When depth > 0, the function will follow child links (links with x as a prefix) and collect links from those pages as well.

children_only

Logical or string. If TRUE, returns only child links (those having x as a prefix). If FALSE, returns all links found on the page. Note that regardless of this setting, only child links are followed when depth > 0.

progress

Logical, draw a progress bar if depth > 0.

...

Currently unused. Must be empty.

url_filter

A function that takes a character vector of URL's and may subset them to return a smaller list. This can be useful for filtering out URL's by rules different than children_only which only checks the prefix.

validate

Default is FALSE. If TRUE, checks that local files exist and sends a HEAD request for each remote link, removing those that are not accessible. Requests are sent in parallel using httr2::req_perform_parallel().

get_timestamps

Default is FALSE. If TRUE, sends parallel HEAD requests for any discovered URLs that were not visited during crawling, and records their Last-Modified response header. Sitemap <lastmod> dates and datetimes are recorded without extra requests; only missing or invalid sitemap dates need HEAD requests. Pages fetched during crawling use the GET response header when present and retain their sitemap date otherwise. Useful for incremental ingest: callers can skip re-fetching pages whose timestamp has not changed since the last run. Note that not all hosting platforms set Last-Modified; S3-backed sites (including many docs.posit.co pages) and GitHub Pages do, while Netlify-hosted sites (e.g. quarto.org) do not. Missing headers and local file timestamps are recorded as NA.

include_root

Default is FALSE. If TRUE, also includes the starting page in the results, subject to children_only, url_filter, and validate. Sitemap inputs contribute only their listed URLs. If FALSE, the starting page can still be returned when it is found through a link.

metadata

Default is FALSE. If TRUE, returns a tibble with a character source column and a POSIXct last_modified column, with one row per returned link. Missing timestamps are NA. This does not request additional timestamps; use get_timestamps = TRUE for that.

Value

By default, a ragnar_links object: a character vector of URLs, sorted alphabetically and deduplicated, with the following attributes:

last_modified

A named POSIXct vector of timestamps from response headers and sitemap entries. Always present. URLs without a known timestamp are NA or absent from this vector; metadata = TRUE gives every returned link a row with NA for an unknown timestamp.

problems

A data frame with columns link and problem, present when a link could not be fetched or validated, or a sitemap entry lacks an absolute HTTP(S) URL.

Joins and row-binding combine links as ordinary character vectors. To keep timestamps in the combined data, use metadata = TRUE. This returns a tibble with source and last_modified columns in the same order as the default vector. Both return types retain the problems attribute when present, including problems for links excluded from the results.

Examples

# \dontrun{
ragnar_find_links("https://r4ds.hadley.nz/base-R.html")
#> # A ragnar_links vector: 88 URLs
#>    url                                                  last_modified
#> 1  https://adv-r.hadley.nz/subsetting.html              <NA>         
#> 2  https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/across.html    <NA>         
#> 3  https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/arrange.html   <NA>         
#> 4  https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/filter.html    <NA>         
#> 5  https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/group_by.html  <NA>         
#> 6  https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/mutate.html    <NA>         
#> 7  https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/pull.html      <NA>         
#> 8  https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/relocate.html  <NA>         
#> 9  https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/select.html    <NA>         
#> 10 https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/summarise.html <NA>         
#> # ... with 78 more rows
ragnar_find_links("https://ellmer.tidyverse.org/")

ragnar_find_links(
  paste0("https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/sfquickstarts/",
         "tree/master/site/sfguides/src/build_a_custom_model_for_anomaly_detection"),
  children_only = "https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/sfquickstarts",
  depth = 1
)
#> Error in open.connection(con, open = mode): cannot open the connection

# Retrieve Last-Modified timestamps for all discovered URLs
links <- ragnar_find_links(
  "https://docs.posit.co/",
  children_only = TRUE,
  depth = 1,
  get_timestamps = TRUE,
  metadata = TRUE
)
